messages:
tara: quick async check — noticed a 95p latency bump on the gateway canary after the kernel prefetch change landed (canary g-41). Anyone owning the prefetch/kv-path today? need quick ownership and rollback plan if this is real :warning:

sanjay: i'm on it, looking at traces now. initial suspicion: prefetch fusion with the new continuous-batch scheduler created a small hot-spot in the kernel loop. digging heap/threads. can you paste the canary trace id?

tara: trace GC-20250325-0415 (from dashboard). p95 went from ~85ms to ~210ms on requests with sequence lengths >1024. lower seqs seem fine.

alex: re: ownership, alex and i picked up kernel-prefetch last week but i'm OOO tomorrow morning. alex: are you available to coordinate a quick revert if needed?

alex: i can be primary for rollback/short-term mitigation. if we need rollback, target is reverting commit 9b7f2e3 (PR #4721). i'll prep the revert PR now.

marie: FYI the canary had a small spike at 04:12 UTC and then another at 04:20. I ran a micro-bench against the prefetch branch locally and saw the same regression when batch sizes hit ~64+. attaching snippet of my synthetic run: ```
$ ./bench/throughput --model small --seq 1200 --batch 64
median: 72ms
p95: 198ms
p99: 320ms
```

sanjay: nice repro, thanks. can you upload your local flamegraph to the run artifacts? that will help show kernel loop hotspot.

marie: uploaded to the thread: https://artifacts.redwood/gc/2025/prefetch-flame-0415.svg

ci-bot: deploy-gateway-canary: canary g-41 -> revision v2025-03-25-9 deployed at 04:05 UTC (sha:9b7f2e3). no automated rollback triggered.

sanjay: looking at flamegraph — the KV cache handshake moved into the hot path after fusion. small fix options: 1) move handshake back to background task, 2) add a fast-path check for cached prefix, 3) limit max batch size for fused scheduler on canary.

tara: preference order: 2 (fast-path) if low-risk, else 3 (config change) for immediate mitigation while alex preps revert. which is fastest to ship?

alex: fast-path requires a tiny kernel change but needs CI perf run; might be ~2-3 hours. config limit is trivial (runtime flag) and can ship in 15-30m with hot reload. i'll open the flag PR now and toggle on canary for g-41 only.

marie: if we do the flag route, can someone add a metric for effective batch size after scheduler so we can watch impact? i can add that as a short follow-up.

sanjay: agree. i'll open an issue to track metric + postmortem: https://issues.redwood/INF-1189

tara: plan then — alex pushes config-flag PR to limit fused batch max to 32 on canary. sanjay + marie will watch stacks and metrics. alex prepares revert PR as backup. if p95 doesn't improve in 20m after flag flip, escalate to rollback. i'm pausing non-critical kernel merges until we confirm. :+1:

alex: PR created: https://git.redwood/repo/PR/4783 — toggles fused_batch_max on canary. applying now.

ci-bot: ci: PR #4783 passed unit + integration, perf check pending.

marie: flipped flag on g-41 at 04:36 UTC. within 5m saw p95 drop to ~92ms. dashboard link: https://dashboards.redwood/runtime/canary/g-41

sanjay: confirmed — p95 back to baseline on the canary. leaving monitoring on for 2h. tagging INF-1189 and will capture timeline.

tara: excellent. action items: alex finish revert PR (as backup) -> link it in INF-1189, marie add effective-batch metric, sanjay own postmortem draft. i'll follow up in next standup. thanks team :heart:

alex: revert PR ready at https://git.redwood/repo/PR/4784 (do not merge unless rollback needed).

ci-bot: ticket INF-1189 updated: watchers: tara, sanjay, alex, marie.

tara: tagging owners for clarity: @alex (rollback + config), @sanjay (traces + postmortem), @marie (bench + metric). if anything regresses ping here immediately.
